== APPRAISAL INSTRUCTIONS (GEMINI_HANDOFF_BRIEF §3 Task D; RISK_OF_BIAS.md §§1-2; APPRAISAL_FORM.md; CODEBOOK.md §8) ==
1. ACCESSIBILITY GATE:
   - If `Retrieval status` is `not_accessible` (or the paper text below says `[FULL TEXT NOT ACCESSIBLE]`), you MUST set `paper_read = "not accessible"`, `study_design_identified = "cannot_tell (full text not accessible)"`, `chosen_tool = "cannot_tell"`, `why_tool_chosen = "full text not accessible"`, `overall_rating = "cannot_tell"`, `domain_ratings = []`, all 7 `cross_tool_domains` fields to `"cannot_tell"`, `overall_narrative_summary = "Full text not accessible; no risk-of-bias appraisal performed."`, `where_found_summary = "not accessible"`, and `evidence_quotes = []`. NEVER guess study design or bias ratings from citation/title!

2. STEP 1 — INDEPENDENT DESIGN CLASSIFICATION & TOOL SELECTION (`RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1):
   Classify the study's actual design from its Methods section, then select the matching appraisal tool:
   - `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"`: Individually randomized controlled trial. Rate all 5 domains (`D1` Randomization process; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"`: Cluster-randomized trial (villages, compounds, neighbourhoods, schools, utilities randomized as clusters). Rate all 6 domains (`D1a` Randomization process; `D1b` Timing of identification or recruitment of participants within clusters; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"ROBINS-I"`: Non-randomized study of an intervention / policy with a genuine comparator (DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, comparative longitudinal/panel evaluation). Rate all 7 domains (`D1` Bias due to confounding; `D2` Bias in selection of participants into the study; `D3` Bias in classification of interventions; `D4` Bias due to deviations from intended interventions; `D5` Bias due to missing data; `D6` Bias in measurement of outcomes; `D7` Bias in selection of the reported result — note `No information` honestly if no pre-analysis plan/protocol exists) as `"Low"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Serious"`, `"Critical"`, or `"No information"`, and overall rating in the same vocabulary. Do NOT assign single-case histories with no comparator arm to ROBINS-I!
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"`: Quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without a quasi-experimental intervention structure. Rate all 8 items (`Q1` Inclusion criteria in sample clearly defined; `Q2` Study subjects and setting described in detail; `Q3` Exposure measured validly and reliably; `Q4` Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of condition; `Q5` Confounding factors identified; `Q6` Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly and reliably; `Q8` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`. Provide overall narrative judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, or `"High concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"`: Observational comparative cohort design (not framed as a ROBINS-I intervention). Rate all 11 items (`Q1` Similar groups from same population; `Q2` Exposures measured similarly; `Q3` Exposure measured validly/reliably; `Q4` Confounding factors identified; `Q5` Strategies to deal with confounding stated; `Q6` Participants free of outcome at start; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly/reliably; `Q8` Follow-up time reported and sufficient; `Q9` Follow-up complete or loss explored; `Q10` Strategies to address incomplete follow-up utilized; `Q11` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`, plus narrative overall judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, `"High concern"`).
   - `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"`: Primary qualitative study (interviews, ethnography, focus groups, qualitative documentary/field case study). Rate all 10 items (`Q1` Clear statement of aims; `Q2` Qualitative methodology appropriate; `Q3` Research design appropriate to address aims; `Q4` Recruitment strategy appropriate to aims; `Q5` Data collected in a way that addressed research issue; `Q6` Relationship between researcher and participants adequately considered [reflexivity]; `Q7` Ethical issues considered; `Q8` Data analysis sufficiently rigorous; `Q9` Clear statement of findings; `Q10` How valuable is the research [narrative assessment]). Rate Q1-Q9 `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`, and Q10 narratively; give narrative `overall_rating` (e.g. `"Low methodological concern"`, `"Moderate concern (X Can't tell / No items)"`, `"High methodological concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"`: Genuine mixed-methods primary study combining qualitative AND quantitative empirical components (do NOT assign purely quantitative or purely qualitative studies to MMAT). Rate Screening `S1`-`S2`, Qualitative `1.1`-`1.5`, the matching Quantitative 5-item block (`2.1`-`2.5` randomized, `3.1`-`3.5` non-randomized, or `4.1`-`4.5` descriptive), AND Mixed-Methods integration `5.1`-`5.5` (`5.1` adequate rationale for mixed methods; `5.2` components effectively integrated; `5.3` outputs of integration adequately interpreted; `5.4` divergences/inconsistencies adequately addressed; `5.5` components adhere to quality criteria of each tradition) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`. Per MMAT 2018 rules, NEVER compute a numeric score; provide a concise criterion-grounded narrative `overall_rating` noting that overall quality cannot exceed the weakest component.
   - `"AMSTAR 2"`: Secondary systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with an explicit systematic search/screening method (NEVER apply AMSTAR 2 to non-systematic narrative literature reviews!). Rate all 16 items `Q1`-`Q16` (explicitly marking critical domains `Q2`, `Q4`, `Q7`, `Q9`, `Q11`, `Q13`, `Q15`) as `"Yes"`, `"Partial Yes"` (where applicable), `"No"`, or `"Not applicable (no meta-analysis)"`, and apply AMSTAR 2 overall confidence (`"High"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Low"`, `"Critically Low"`).
   - `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"`: Doctrinal-empirical hybrid, jurimetric analysis, or institutional/legal-historical case study that fits NONE of the six conventional designs above. Rate all 13 narrative domains (`D1` Legal source accuracy; `D2` Jurisdictional specificity; `D3` Exposure definition; `D4` Outcome definition; `D5` Sampling transparency; `D6` Selection process; `D7` Measurement transparency; `D8` Causal identification; `D9` Treatment of confounding; `D10` Institutional context; `D11` Replication potential; `D12` Coding transparency; `D13` Researcher reflexivity) as `"strong"`, `"adequate"`, `"weak"`, or `"not assessable"`. Explicitly frame `overall_rating` as a structured non-validated judgment (NEVER a numeric composite score!).
   - `"NONE"`: Use when the study fits NONE of the listed instruments (e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model with no empirical sample, or non-systematic narrative essay/review with no primary empirical method and no systematic search). Set `overall_rating = "NOT APPLICABLE (design fits no listed tool)"`, explain clearly in `why_tool_chosen` and `overall_narrative_summary` rather than forcing an inappropriate checklist, and still fill the 7 `cross_tool_domains` honestly from the paper!

3. STEP 2 — CROSS-TOOL SUMMARY DOMAINS (`CODEBOOK.md` §8) & VERBATIM QUOTES:
   - Populate `selection_bias`, `measurement_bias`, `confounding`, `attrition`, `reporting_bias`, `legal_measurement_quality` (how rigorously the legal/administrative/institutional rule or exposure was operationalized), and `outcome_measurement_quality` (how rigorously the water/sanitation outcome was measured).

cross_tool_domains.attrition: Not applicable / Unclear (secondary systematic review of 28 cross-sectional primary studies with no longitudinal follow-up; however, 13 full-text exclusions in Figure 1 lack an itemized list with study-specific exclusion reasons).
cross_tool_domains.confounding: High concern (all 28 included primary studies were cross-sectional, and the review's generic summed quality score in Table 1 did not evaluate control for confounding in primary analyses of socio-economic, tenure, or reliability determinants).
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Weak / Descriptive only (legal, regulatory, and institutional variables—such as land tenure, illegal network connections, mandatory fixed utility tariffs during supply interruptions, and fragmented or absent regulation of private wells and water vendors—were not systematically coded or verified against primary legal sources, appearing only as narrative observations drawn from included studies on pp. 10, 12-13, and 16).
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: Moderate to high concern (data extraction was not reported as performed in duplicate, and definitions of water supply reliability, coping strategies, time valuation, and coping cost units varied substantially across primary studies without standardized measurement criteria, pp. 2, 13, 16).
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Moderate concern (household coping strategies were systematically organized into 15 actions across 5 thematic categories in Table 3, but coping costs, water quantities, willingness to pay, and health/water-quality outcomes relied on heterogeneous, mostly self-reported cross-sectional measures without duplicate extraction verification, pp. 10-16).
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: High concern (no pre-registered review protocol or pre-analysis plan was reported, publication bias was not formally assessed in the narrative synthesis despite searching first 50 Google/Google Scholar hits for grey literature, and findings from high-risk-of-bias studies were integrated uncritically alongside low-risk studies).
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: High concern (literature searching and screening were not performed in duplicate by two independent reviewers, search dates were omitted, full-text inclusion was restricted to English without methodological justification, 13 excluded full-text papers were not listed, and several included primary studies used convenience or snowball sampling, pp. 3-5, 16, 18).

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the research questions and inclusion criteria for the review include the components of PICO?
domain_ratings.justification: For an observational exposure/response systematic review, the review clearly specifies the population (households/domestic water users in developing countries per 2012 World Bank classification), exposure/condition (unreliable performance or functionality of household water supply systems), and outcomes (coping strategies, coping costs and socio-economic distribution, health/social outcomes, and strategy effectiveness) in the review questions and selection criteria.

domain_ratings.domain_name: [CRITICAL] Did the report of the review contain an explicit statement that the review methods were established prior to the conduct of the review and did the report justify any significant deviations from the protocol?
domain_ratings.justification: The paper contains no statement of an a priori review protocol or registration (e.g., PROSPERO) for this review and reports no protocol deviations (the only protocol mentioned on p. 4 is Hellebrandt et al. [26], from which the authors adapted their quality appraisal rubric).
domain_ratings.where_found: Section 2 (PDF pp. 2-4) and Author Contributions (PDF p. 18)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the review authors explain their selection of the study designs for inclusion in the review?
domain_ratings.justification: Section 2.2 states only that included papers had to be 'Based on empirical research' and excluded papers that listed coping strategies without supporting detail, without explaining or justifying the selection or unrestricted inclusion of specific empirical study designs.

domain_ratings.domain_name: [CRITICAL] Did the review authors use a comprehensive literature search strategy?
domain_ratings.justification: Although the authors searched seven electronic databases (CINAHL EBSCOHost, Embase Ovid, PubMed Central, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Scirus, Web of Knowledge), provided the exact Boolean search string, checked reference lists, and searched grey literature via the first 50 hits in Google and Google Scholar, they restricted full-text inclusion to English-language papers without methodological justification (merely noting it as a limitation on p. 16), omitted the dates when searches were conducted, and did not report consulting content experts or study registries. Under strict AMSTAR 2 criteria requiring justification of language restrictions even for Partial Yes, this domain is rated No.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the review authors perform study selection in duplicate?
domain_ratings.justification: Methods do not report independent duplicate screening of titles/abstracts or full texts, and Author Contributions state that a single author (Batsirai Majuru) performed the literature search and drafted the manuscript.
domain_ratings.where_found: Section 2.2 (PDF pp. 3-4) and Author Contributions (PDF p. 18)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the review authors perform data extraction in duplicate?
domain_ratings.justification: No procedure for independent duplicate data extraction or consensus checking by a second reviewer is reported anywhere in the Methods or Author Contributions sections.
domain_ratings.where_found: Section 2.2-2.4 (PDF pp. 3-4) and Author Contributions (PDF p. 18)

domain_ratings.domain_name: [CRITICAL] Did the review authors provide a list of excluded studies and justify the exclusions?
domain_ratings.justification: Figure 1 reports that 37 full texts were screened and 13 studies were excluded as 'not fully meeting inclusion criteria', but no bibliographic list of those 13 excluded full-text studies or study-specific exclusion justifications is provided.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the review authors describe the included studies in adequate detail?
domain_ratings.justification: Table 2 describes each of the 28 included studies' objectives, urban/rural setting and country, water supply type, and sampling strategy/sample size, and Table 3 maps coping strategies per study; however, study timeframes, detailed exposure gradations, comparator structures, and numerical effect estimates are not systematically tabulated for all studies, satisfying Partial Yes rather than full Yes.
domain_ratings.where_found: Section 3, Table 2 (PDF pp. 7-9), and Table 3 (PDF p. 11)

domain_ratings.domain_name: [CRITICAL] Did the review authors use a satisfactory technique for assessing the risk of bias (RoB) in individual studies that were included in the review?
domain_ratings.justification: Rather than using design-appropriate risk-of-bias tools evaluating confounding, selection bias, exposure/outcome measurement validity, and selective reporting in non-randomized/observational studies, the authors assigned arbitrary numeric scores across six broad reporting/validity headings and summed them into a composite score (0-12) to label overall risk of bias Low (10-12), Moderate (7-9), or High (<=6) in Table 1—contrary to both AMSTAR 2 standards and the Hellebrandt et al. framework they adapted.
domain_ratings.where_found: Section 2.3 (PDF p. 4), Section 3 (PDF p. 5), and Table 1 (PDF p. 6)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the review authors report on the sources of funding for the studies included in the review?
domain_ratings.justification: While World Bank funding is mentioned incidentally in the conceptual background for early studies [15, 18, 21], the review does not systematically report funding sources for the 28 included studies in Table 2 or the Results text.

domain_ratings.domain_name: [CRITICAL] If meta-analysis was performed did the review authors use appropriate methods for statistical combination of results?
domain_ratings.justification: No meta-analysis or quantitative pooling was performed; due to heterogeneity across disciplines, study designs, and cost metrics, the authors conducted a thematic narrative synthesis.

domain_ratings.domain_name: If meta-analysis was performed, did the review authors assess the potential impact of RoB in individual studies on the results of the meta-analysis or other evidence synthesis?
[CRITICAL] Did the review authors account for RoB in individual studies when interpreting/ discussing the results of the review?
domain_ratings.justification: Although Table 1 classifies three studies ([16/17], [29], [44]) as High risk of bias and 13 as Moderate risk of bias, Sections 3.1-3.5 and Section 4 repeatedly draw substantive findings on coping mechanisms, hygiene/contamination impacts, mandatory bills, and collective action from high-risk studies (especially Chaminuka & Nyatsanza [29] and Jamal & Rahman [44]) without weighting, stratifying, or qualifying those specific inferences by study risk of bias.
domain_ratings.where_found: Table 1 (PDF p. 6), Sections 3.1-3.5 (PDF pp. 10-14), and Section 4 (PDF pp. 15-17)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the review authors provide a satisfactory explanation for, and discussion of, any heterogeneity observed in the results of the review?
domain_ratings.justification: The authors explicitly examine and explain substantial variation across studies in coping cost-to-income ratios (e.g., 1% in Nepal vs. 12% in Kenya and 15% among low-income Indian households) and divergences between coping costs and willingness to pay (higher WTP than coping costs in Nepal vs. lower WTP in India, Pakistan, and Trinidad and Tobago), attributing heterogeneity to local hydrogeology/drilling costs, differing cost components measured, affordability constraints, erosion of trust in utilities, and prior household investments in large storage tanks.

domain_ratings.domain_name: [CRITICAL] If they performed quantitative synthesis did the review authors carry out an adequate investigation of publication bias (small study bias) and discuss its likely impact on the results of the review?
domain_ratings.justification: No quantitative synthesis or meta-analysis was conducted.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the review authors report any potential sources of conflict of interest, including any funding they received for conducting the review?
domain_ratings.justification: The manuscript includes an explicit 'Conflicts of Interest: The authors declare no conflict of interest' statement at the end of the text, meeting AMSTAR 2 Q16 criteria for reporting no competing interests (though external review funding is not separately stated).

raw_response.overall_narrative_summary: Majuru, Suhrcke, and Hunter (2016) is a systematic review with thematic narrative synthesis (no meta-analysis) of 28 empirical cross-sectional studies examining household coping strategies, coping costs, socio-economic distribution, and effectiveness in response to unreliable domestic water supplies in developing countries. Appraised with AMSTAR 2, overall confidence in the review's results is Critically Low due to multiple flaws in critical domains: no a priori review protocol or registration was stated (Q2); full-text eligibility was restricted to English without methodological justification and search dates were omitted (Q4); the 13 full-text articles excluded after screening were not listed with individual reasons (Q7); individual study quality was appraised by summing arbitrary points across six broad reporting/validity items into a composite 0-12 score rather than evaluating domain-specific confounding, selection, and measurement biases appropriate to observational designs (Q9); and findings from studies rated High risk of bias were synthesized uncritically alongside Low-risk studies without sensitivity discussion (Q13). Additional non-critical weaknesses include lack of duplicate study selection (Q5) and duplicate data extraction (Q6), lack of justification for study design inclusion (Q3), and non-reporting of primary study funding sources (Q10). Key strengths are well-defined review questions and eligibility criteria (Q1), multi-database searching including grey literature and reference lists, structured tabular description of included studies and 15 coping strategies (Q8), thoughtful explanation of heterogeneity in coping costs and willingness-to-pay estimates across settings (Q14), and an explicit conflict-of-interest declaration (Q16).
raw_response.study_design_identified: Systematic review (thematic narrative synthesis of 28 cross-sectional quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods empirical studies; no meta-analysis)
raw_response.where_found_summary: Methods in Sections 2.1-2.4 (PDF pp. 2-4); screening flowchart Figure 1 and risk-of-bias Table 1 in Section 3 (PDF pp. 4-6); study characteristics in Table 2 (PDF pp. 7-9) and coping strategies matrix in Table 3 (PDF p. 11); thematic synthesis in Sections 3.1-3.5 (PDF pp. 10-14); limitations, regulatory context, and heterogeneity discussion in Section 4 (PDF pp. 15-17); Author Contributions and Conflicts of Interest on PDF p. 18.
raw_response.why_tool_chosen: S438 is a secondary systematic review featuring a structured multi-database Boolean search strategy, explicit eligibility criteria, a PRISMA-style screening flow diagram (1,643 initial records to 28 included studies), and formal study quality assessment, making AMSTAR 2 the exact required instrument under RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1 (with meta-analysis items Q11, Q12, and Q15 marked Not applicable because synthesis is purely thematic/narrative).
